units.title: My classroom: words for everyday things
units.prerequisites: None; optional Vietnamese labels for new learners
units.goal: Recognise five common school words in short everyday contexts and match each word to its use; no CEFR level awarded.
units.concept: Use a word together with a simple action. bag = carry books; door = enter or leave; chair = sit; desk = work or write; teacher = help learners in class. Say the words, then cover the bank before practice. Written text and optional Vietnamese support are available; pictures/audio are not required to answer.
units.support_vi: Ghép từ với hành động: bag = cặp, door = cửa ra vào, chair = ghế, desk = bàn học, teacher = giáo viên. Có thể xem từ gợi ý lúc đầu, sau đó che lại khi làm bài.
units.model: Different model words (not scored): The board is at the front of the room. A window lets light in. Notice how each word is connected to a useful description.
strategy: Read the short sentence and imagine the action.
Decide whether you need a person, place or object.
Try to remember the word before looking at the choices.
units.hint: Is the sentence about carrying, closing, sitting, writing or helping learners?
units.feedback_strategy: After Submit, reread the whole sentence, name the action and compare the meanings of the wrong options. Try one new sentence without looking at the word bank.

practice.prompt: I carry my books to school in my ___.

feedback.explanation_en: A bag is something you can carry books in.

practice.prompt: Please close the ___ when you leave the room.

feedback.explanation_en: A door can be closed when someone leaves a room.

practice.prompt: We sit on a ___ in class.

feedback.explanation_en: A chair is for sitting on.

practice.prompt: We put our notebooks on the ___ to write.

feedback.explanation_en: A desk is a surface for writing.

practice.prompt: The ___ helps us learn new words.

feedback.explanation_en: A teacher is a person who helps learners.

units.title: Can I have it, please?
units.goal: Use a memorised polite request, response and thanks in a familiar classroom situation.
units.concept: A simple polite request has a useful pattern: Can I have + thing + please? A person may reply Here you are. Then say Thank you. This is supported formula practice, not proof of independent conversation skill.
units.support_vi: Mẫu câu lịch sự: Can I have ... , please? = Cho mình xin ... được không? Here you are = Đây nhé. Thank you = Cảm ơn.
units.model: Different model: Kim asks, 'Can I have the green crayon, please?' Jo gives it and says, 'Here you are.' Kim replies, 'Thank you!'
strategy: Identify what you need.
Choose a short polite request rather than a command.
When someone helps, reply with thanks.
units.hint: Look for Can I ... please? and a friendly reply.
units.feedback_strategy: If you selected a command, compare how it sounds with a polite request. Repeat the three-part exchange using a different classroom object.

practice.prompt: You need a ruler. Which request is polite?

options.text: Can I have a ruler, please?

feedback.explanation_en: Can I have ... please? is a polite way to ask.

practice.prompt: A friend gives you a pencil. What can you say?

feedback.explanation_en: Thank you acknowledges help politely.

practice.prompt: A friend asks for the eraser and you give it. What can you say?

feedback.explanation_en: Here you are is a natural reply when handing something over.

practice.prompt: Complete the polite request with ONE word: Can I ___ the blue pen, please?

feedback.explanation_en: Can I have ... please? asks for an object politely.

practice.prompt: Which is a polite way to ask for the paper?

feedback.explanation_en: Please makes the request more courteous.

units.title: Write a short friendly invitation
units.goal: Plan and write a friendly invitation containing an activity, day/time, clear meeting point and ending.
units.concept: Before writing, check who will read the message and what they need to know. Use greeting → invitation → day/time → meeting place → friendly ending. Do not include private addresses, phone numbers or passwords. A checklist helps but does not automatically grade the writing.
units.support_vi: Xác định người nhận, hoạt động, ngày giờ và địa điểm gặp. Viết lời chào → lời mời → thời gian → điểm hẹn → kết thúc. Không ghi thông tin cá nhân.
units.model: Different task model: Hi Ben! Would you like to help me plant flowers on Sunday? Let's meet at the park entrance at nine. See you there! — This example is not the board-game task below.
strategy: List the four details the reader needs.
Choose a friendly greeting and clear order.
Write short complete sentences; check time and place.
Reread for missing information and privacy.
units.hint: Who, what activity, when, where, and a friendly closing?
units.feedback_strategy: Objective planning questions have explanations after Submit. The message itself is saved for authorised human feedback and revision; no automatic CEFR/writing score.

practice.prompt: What information helps a friend act on an invitation?

feedback.explanation_en: An invitation needs enough practical details to plan a visit.

practice.prompt: Which opening suits a friendly message to a classmate?

options.text: Hi Noor! Would you like to come?

feedback.explanation_en: A classmate needs a friendly and clear invitation.

practice.prompt: Which sentence gives a specific meeting time?

feedback.explanation_en: 4:30 p.m. is a specific time rather than a vague suggestion.

practice.prompt: Write 35–55 words to invite a classmate to play a board game at the community centre on Friday at 4:30 p.m. Include a clear meeting point and a friendly closing. Use an invented first name; do not share private contact details.

feedback.pending_message: Saved for authorised adult review. Revise after feedback; completion alone is not proof of writing level.

units.title: Plan a polite classroom request
units.goal: Prepare keywords for a simple request, choose a polite sentence and optionally practise aloud without claiming observed speech.
units.concept: A useful plan is: greeting or excuse me → request → short reason (optional) → thank you. Keep 3–4 keywords, not a full script. Speaking aloud and self-checking are voluntary practice; no oral fluency, pronunciation or CEFR score is produced.
units.support_vi: Chỉ chuẩn bị 3–4 từ khóa cho lời đề nghị lịch sự, không bắt buộc ghi âm. Tự luyện nói không được tính là điểm năng lực nói.
units.model: Different model: 'Excuse me. Could I borrow the green marker for my poster, please? Thank you.' Keywords: marker → poster → please → thanks.
strategy: Choose the item or help you need.
Make a polite request using Could I ...? or Could you ...?
Use keywords, then practise once aloud if comfortable.
Mark self-report honestly; this is not an evaluated recording.
units.hint: A polite request asks for help and avoids commands.
units.feedback_strategy: Objective selections can show language-knowledge explanations, but all oral competence evidence remains weight 0. A self-report is labelled Self-Reported Practice, not a passed speaking test.

practice.prompt: You need to borrow a ruler. Which request is polite?

options.text: Could I borrow a ruler, please?

feedback.explanation_en: Could I borrow ... please? asks politely.

practice.prompt: You did not hear the instruction. What could you say?

options.text: Could you say that again, please?

feedback.explanation_en: A polite clarification request is useful when you did not hear.

practice.prompt: Which plan helps you speak naturally?

options.text: Read a long paragraph without looking up

feedback.explanation_en: A short keyword plan supports an understandable request.

practice.prompt: Write up to four safe keywords for asking to borrow a ruler for class. If you wish, say your request aloud once, then mark whether you practised. No microphone, recording or personal information is required.

feedback.pending_message: Self-Reported Practice only. No automated pronunciation, fluency or CEFR score.

units.title: Two updates: which rule applies now?
units.prerequisites: A1 reading of dates, places and simple conditions; P01-U03 helpful
units.goal: Compare an original notice with an update and apply the newest instructions to a new learner case.
units.concept: Read each notice for its date and purpose. The newest update may replace only some details. Make two columns: old plan and current plan. Words such as instead, now, extended and already tell you what changed and who is affected.
units.support_vi: Đọc hai thông báo theo thứ tự thời gian, so sánh kế hoạch cũ và mới. Chú ý instead, now, extended, already để hiểu thay đổi và ngoại lệ.
units.model: Independent mini-update: Book Swap was planned for Table 5 at 2:30. A later message says it will be at Table 8 at 3:00 because the hall is busy. The new place and time replace the old ones; nothing else is stated to change.
strategy: Read the original notice for the basic plan.
Read the update and mark each changed field.
Keep unchanged details from the original.
Apply any rule about people who already registered.
units.hint: Which notice is later? Does the update replace this detail or leave it unchanged?
units.feedback_strategy: After Submit, identify the exact update sentence. For an error, make a two-column old/new table and explain which rule applies to a learner who already signed up.
units.assessed_text: NOTICE — Monday: The Makers Club meets on Wednesday in Studio 2 at 3:30 p.m. Bring a clean jar for the project. Registration closes on Monday at 6 p.m. UPDATE — Tuesday morning: Studio 2 is being painted. This Wednesday the club will meet in Workshop 4 at 4:00 p.m. Bring old newspapers instead of a jar. Registration is now open until Tuesday at 7 p.m. Anyone who registered before the update does not need to register again.

practice.prompt: Where should students go this Wednesday?

feedback.explanation_en: The Tuesday update changes the location to Workshop 4.

practice.prompt: What time does the updated meeting start?

feedback.explanation_en: The update gives 4:00 p.m. as the new start time.

practice.prompt: What should students bring after the update?

feedback.explanation_en: The words instead of replace the jar with newspapers.

practice.prompt: What is the new registration deadline?

feedback.explanation_en: The update extends registration until Tuesday at 7 p.m.

practice.prompt: Why is the meeting place different?

feedback.explanation_en: The updated notice states Studio 2 is being painted.

practice.prompt: Sam registered on Monday. Must Sam register again?

options.text: Yes, only new students may attend

feedback.explanation_en: The update explicitly exempts people who already registered.

units.title: Suggest, disagree and clarify in a group
units.prerequisites: Simple polite requests and A1 school collaboration vocabulary
units.goal: Choose natural phrases to suggest an idea, disagree politely, ask for clarification and agree in a group task.
units.concept: Useful collaboration chunks: Could we ...? (suggest); I see your point, but ... (polite difference); What do you mean by ...? (clarify); Shall we ...? (suggest shared action); That works for me. (agree). Identify the communication purpose before choosing a phrase.
units.support_vi: Phân biệt chức năng giao tiếp: đề xuất, bất đồng lịch sự, hỏi lại cho rõ và đồng ý. Học cả cụm từ thay vì từng từ đơn lẻ.
units.model: Different model: 'We could design a garden sign.' — 'I see your point, but we have no paint. Could we use coloured paper instead?' — 'That works for me.' This is not the assessed poster/science-project situation.
strategy: Identify the speaker's intention.
Select a complete natural chunk for that intention.
Check that the phrase is polite and fits the previous sentence.
units.hint: Is the speaker proposing an idea, gently disagreeing, asking what something means, or agreeing?
units.feedback_strategy: After Submit, label each wrong option with the communication action it actually expresses; practise a new context without looking at the toolkit.

practice.prompt: Your team has no plan for a science poster. Which phrase makes a suggestion?

options.text: Could we draw a diagram first?
I do not know where my shoes are.

feedback.explanation_en: Could we ...? is a polite way to propose a plan.

practice.prompt: A friend suggests a very large model, but the table is small. Which reply disagrees politely?

options.text: I see your point, but the table is too small.

feedback.explanation_en: I see your point, but ... acknowledges the idea and gives a reason.

practice.prompt: You do not understand 'sort the cards by theme'. What should you ask?

feedback.explanation_en: What do you mean by ...? requests clarification.

practice.prompt: A classmate suggests a sensible order and you agree. What can you say?

feedback.explanation_en: That works for me expresses agreement.

practice.prompt: Complete with ONE word: ___ we try a smaller model?

feedback.explanation_en: Could we ...? and Shall we ...? both make a suggestion.

practice.prompt: Write one original polite suggestion for your own group project and one polite response. This is optional free use and is NOT auto-scored for meaning.

feedback.pending_message: Saved as optional unassessed transfer; request human feedback for naturalness.

units.title: Ask for help with a project problem
units.prerequisites: A1 invitation structure and A2 reason-giving phrases
units.goal: Write a short polite message explaining a practical problem, why it matters and one clear request.
units.concept: A useful help request has: greeting → problem → why it matters → specific request → thanks. State facts you know; avoid blaming people or inventing details. Check that your reader knows what action to take. The message itself requires human review, not automatic proficiency scoring.
units.support_vi: Viết lời chào → nêu vấn đề → giải thích ảnh hưởng → đề nghị giúp đỡ cụ thể → cảm ơn. Không tự bịa thông tin và không ghi dữ liệu cá nhân.
units.model: Different model: 'Hello Mr Kim, I cannot find the history worksheet for Tuesday. I checked our class folder. Could you tell me where I can get a copy? Thank you, Mai.' The assessed task below is about a science-fair display board.
strategy: Write one factual sentence about the problem.
Explain why it affects the planned activity.
Ask for one realistic action using Could you ...?
Check friendly tone, clarity, grammar and privacy.
units.hint: What went wrong? Why does it matter? What exactly should the reader do?
units.feedback_strategy: Objective planning checks explain errors. The original message is stored as a draft for authorised adult review using task response, clarity, polite tone and language accuracy; no automatic CEFR/writing score.

practice.prompt: Which order makes a help request easy to follow?

feedback.explanation_en: The reader needs to know what happened and what help is requested.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is a polite request?

options.text: Could you check when the board will arrive?

feedback.explanation_en: Could you ...? asks for a specific action politely.

practice.prompt: Which detail explains why a missing display board matters?

options.text: We need it to show our project at the fair.

feedback.explanation_en: The fair display connects the problem to the task.

practice.prompt: Write 55–80 words to your science-club leader. Your group is preparing for a science fair, but the display board has not arrived. Explain the problem, why it matters and one reasonable request. Use an invented first name and no private contact details.

feedback.pending_message: Saved for authorised adult review. Revise after specific feedback; no automated CEFR or original-writing score.
